meta.title: CPC Utils — portable Windows tools for technicians
meta.description: CPC Utils builds small portable Windows tools: a visual 7-Zip self-extracting package builder and a tool launcher for Windows and WinPE. No installer, no runtime, no account.

hero.sub: Two programs for people who fix machines: a visual builder that turns a folder into one self-extracting exe, and a launcher that carries the same tool list from Windows into WinPE. Both are single portable executables — no installer, no .NET, no runtime.

shotCard.p: Nothing to install, nothing to register: a single exe and its settings folder, on a stick or in a PE image.

shots.alt: CPC 7z SFX Builder extracting a 289 MB package at 55% with the live log
CPC MInst Launcher with grouped tools, search field and the info bar of the selected program

umbrella.h2: Two tools today, one rule for all of them
umbrella.p: Each program does one job and ships as a single portable exe: nothing to install, settings next to it, no account. More tools are in the works.

items: No installer, no .NET, no runtime to add to an image
Runs from a USB stick, a bench machine or a WinPE image
Settings are plain files next to the exe; nothing to register
Delete the folder and the tool is gone

items.a: Yes, and the packages are yours: anything you build with the free edition can be used without limits. Free adds a short branding splash to the package it builds. Pro ($30, perpetual) removes it, adds installer mode and silent packages, and includes 12 months of updates and support.

items.q: Do I need .NET or an installation?
items.a: No. It is one portable exe that talks to the Windows API directly. Copy it to a USB stick, a network share or a WinPE image and run it.
A folder or an existing archive. 7z, zip, rar, tar, cab and iso are all supported, and archive contents are added without recompressing what is already compressed.

items.q: Can I check a package before I ship it?
items.a: Yes. The Check page reports config, content and integrity separately, and only says Passed when every line is green.

Two separate things. The builder itself is being signed with a Microsoft-trusted certificate, so Windows shows Central PC Service as the publisher when you run the tool. A package you build is yours: we do not sign it. You can sign it yourself: the Build page takes a code-signing certificate from the Windows certificate store and adds a timestamp, and then Windows shows your name instead of Unknown publisher. Without a signature Windows shows the usual warning, and the package's own integrity check still catches any later modification.

items.q: What does the Pro edition add?
items.a: Installer mode, silent packages without a window, and no splash screen in the output. The free edition already builds complete packages, and you may use them without limits. The full matrix is on the Pricing page.

items.q: How many languages does the interface have?
items.a: Twelve: German, English, Hungarian, Polish, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Czech, Romanian, Russian and Turkish. Each language is a single file, so the next ones arrive with an update rather than a separate build.

items.q: Does it use 7-Zip's own SFX module?
items.a: No. The extractor inside every package is our own build from the LZMA SDK 24.08 with our patches: a branded splash during long extractions, error messages in plain language instead of raw Win32 codes, and our icon when you do not choose one. The SDK is public domain, so no third-party module decides when your packages get fixed.

items.q: How much do the licences cost?
items.a: CPC 7z SFX Builder is free; Pro is $30 perpetual, with 12 months of updates and an optional $10/year renewal. CPC MInst Launcher is free with every function; Supporter is $20 and Brand $60. Full matrix on the Pricing page.

sfx-builder.title: CPC 7z SFX Builder - self-extracting 7-Zip package builder
sfx-builder.lead: Visual builder for self-extracting 7-Zip packages: folder or archive in, one portable exe out, with installer mode and verification.

sections.h: See every file at a glance
sections.p: The full source list loads root files first, folders A to Z after them. The footer keeps the running file count and the total size, so the size of the job is visible before the build starts.
Pick the program to start, add parameters, a finish message, and preparation steps that run after extraction in the order you choose.
Unpack to Temp, a user folder, ProgramData or beside the package. Deleting the files after the run is a separate switch, so nothing disappears by accident.
Add a wizard, a target folder, desktop and Start-menu shortcuts and an uninstall entry, or keep it a plain portable package. Same project, one switch.
Every package can carry a config signature and a content hash, and the Check page reports config, content and integrity separately.

Twelve languages ship in the current build: German, English, Hungarian, Polish, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Czech, Romanian, Russian and Turkish. Each one is a single text file, so the next ones arrive with an update rather than a new build. The interface comes first, the help follows.

closing.p: Source files, launch settings, installer mode and the Check page sit in the same project. No export, no second tool.

cta.p: No account, no email. The download always points at the current release.

launcher.title: CPC MInst Launcher — one tool list for Windows and WinPE
launcher.lead: Tool list for a service bench: grouped, searchable, one click to launch, same profile in Windows and WinPE. No installer, no runtime.

heroShot.alt: CPC MInst Launcher at its default window size: Windows PE profile, three groups of tools, search field and the info bar of the selected program

sections.p: Backup, Diagnostics, Disk: groups you create, rename, reorder, sort or hide. Nothing depends on where a file happens to sit on disk.
Start typing and the list narrows without pressing Enter; Backspace widens it again. Groups collapse to the matches, so a 200-item stick takes two keystrokes.
The switch at the top swaps the whole list: load, duplicate, rename, delete, import or export. An existing MInstAll collection opens as it is, without rebuilding.
Flag items for WinPE or 64-bit only, and let autorun items start in order, skipping anything whose OS does not match. Settings that make no sense in PE are disabled instead of failing silently.
Every save writes a timestamped backup first. If the backup cannot be written, nothing is saved and you are told why. The last ten backups are kept.
Icons come from the program itself, from the icon library, or from a file you pick. Desktop and Start-menu shortcuts are generated for you, and removed when the item goes.

spotlight.alt: Three partition tools left after typing partition: the search filters the grouped list while the info bar shows size, path and platform
spotlight.h: Two keystrokes instead of a scroll
spotlight.p: Filtering happens on the list you already have, not in a new window. Type a few letters, watch the groups collapse to matching tools, and read the size, path and OS from the info bar.

features.h: The parts you use every day
features.sub: Small things that decide whether a launcher survives a working day.

items.p: After launching it can live in the tray, or snap to the right edge as a narrow tool strip that follows the taskbar.
F10 runs, F2 edits, F3 opens the side bar, Del removes, and the arrow keys move an item inside its group.
An item whose file is missing stays in the list, marked, with the expected path in the info bar.
About 734 KB, settings live next to it, no .NET and no runtime to install.

items.a: Yes, and not as a demo: every function is in the free edition, including WinPE. Supporter ($20) removes the splash screen and shows your name; Brand ($60) puts your own company name and logo in the header, in PE as well. Both are perpetual with 12 months of updates.
It reads and writes the same profile format, so your existing collection opens as it is. It is an independent program, a launcher rather than an installer.
Yes, with the same profile. Autorun items start with the shell; settings that only make sense in Windows, such as starting with the system, are disabled in PE.

items.q: Do I have to rebuild my tool collection?
items.a: No. Load your existing profile and it appears grouped as before. Fields the launcher does not use are preserved when it saves.

items.q: What happens if a tool goes missing?
items.a: The item stays in the list marked as not found, with its path in the info bar. A broken stick is visible before a client sits down.
